problem: Generative object manipulation methods operate in 2D image space and struggle with 3D scene complexities like ambiguous object positioning, orientation, and occlusion relations.
approach: SpatialHand encodes 6DoF pose conditions by decomposing them into 2D location via masked images, depth via composited depth maps, and 3D orientation embedded in latent features, using synthetic data construction and multi-stage training.
contribution: Achieves versatile 6DoF-controllable object insertion with implicit pose encoding superior to existing 2D methods, enabling intuitive AR/VR-like manipulation.

problem: LLM providers must balance performance and cost through model routing, but user behavior and provider incentives may diverge, leading to potential misalignment in model selection and resource allocation.
approach: Models the interaction as a Stackelberg game where an LLM provider routes between standard and reasoning models based on task difficulty while a user decides whether to re-prompt or abandon tasks, solving for optimal policies.
contribution: Reveals that optimal routing typically involves static policies without cascading, identifies misalignment gaps when provider and user preferences differ, and shows conditions where providers may throttle latency to minimize costs.

problem: Writing comprehensive unit tests is challenging, and existing LLM-based methods for automated unit test generation lack effective training strategies to produce high-quality tests.
approach: UTRL trains two LLMs adversarially via reinforcement learning: a test generator maximizing discrimination reward to reveal code faults, and a code generator maximizing code reward to pass the generated tests.
contribution: Qwen3-4B trained with UTRL generates unit tests of higher quality than ground-truth SFT training and outperforms GPT-4.1 and GPT-4o in test quality evaluation.

problem: Deep reinforcement learning is sample-inefficient because policies are optimized directly in high-dimensional, redundant parameter spaces, especially challenging in multi-task settings.
approach: Develops an unsupervised approach that compresses the policy parameter space into a low-dimensional latent space via a generative model trained on behavioral reconstruction loss, enabling policy gradient optimization in latent space.
contribution: Demonstrates compression of policy network parameterization by up to five orders of magnitude while retaining expressivity, and enables task-specific adaptation via latent-space policy gradient.

problem: Continual learning models in mission-critical settings need uncertainty awareness to calibrate predictions, but existing uncertainty-aware methods suffer from high computational overhead and incompatibility with mainstream replay methods.
approach: IDER adapts training loss to make models idempotent on current data streams and introduces idempotence distillation loss that refeeds model output through old checkpoints to minimize distance between reprocessed and original outputs.
contribution: Consistently improves prediction reliability while boosting accuracy and reducing forgetting across CL benchmarks, integrating seamlessly with existing CL approaches.

problem: Incremental object detection suffers from catastrophic forgetting when learning new classes, with task interference poorly modeled because single images contain objects from multiple temporal tasks that may be mislabeled as background.
approach: IKI-EWC framework leverages Elastic Weight Consolidation to estimate task conflicts using old detector mispredictions on new data, derives mathematical relationships between learned and interference knowledge, and uses prototype-based knowledge calibration for classification heads.
contribution: Addresses conflict knowledge preservation through explicit modeling of task interference at the parameter level, enabling incremental learning without forgetting.

problem: Standard time-series forecasting training minimizes mean squared error which provides biased conditional distribution alignment in the presence of label autocorrelation.
approach: DistDF aligns conditional distributions by minimizing a joint-distribution Wasserstein discrepancy, which provably upper bounds the true conditional discrepancy and admits tractable differentiable estimation.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art forecasting performance across diverse models through joint-distribution Wasserstein alignment, improving upon direct forecast approaches.

problem: Despite RL-based reasoning models showing strong capabilities, it is unclear whether comparable reasoning can be elicited from base models at inference time without additional training.
approach: Proposes an iterative sampling algorithm inspired by MCMC techniques that leverages base models' own likelihoods to sample from sharpened distributions without requiring training, curated datasets, or verifiers.
contribution: Achieves substantial reasoning boosts on MATH500, HumanEval, and GPQA that nearly match RL-posttraining while avoiding diversity collapse and enabling broader applicability.

problem: Robotic systems require multimodal reasoning under stringent constraints of latency, memory, and energy, with standard instruction tuning and token-level distillation failing to deliver under these constraints.
approach: BOLT uses option-level decision distillation to align student models directly on multi-choice decision surfaces and budget-aware test-time augmentation that routes low-cost signals to trigger high-resolution reevaluation only when beneficial.
contribution: A 2B student distilled from 13B LLaVA improves accuracy from 28.66% to 50.50% with decision distillation and budgeted routing, surpassing the 13B teacher at 36.74% while reducing GPU memory from 26,878 MB to 3,035 MB.

problem: Collective decision-making effectiveness is challenged by bounded rationality and stochasticity of individual agents aggregating private signals about unknown states.
approach: Models expert behavior using quantal response, a stochastic choice model capturing bounded rationality, and analyzes optimal aggregation within a minimax regret framework using majority voting.
contribution: Shows majority voting is optimal under certain rationality thresholds and that moderately stochastic LLM outputs (via temperature) can outperform perfectly rational agents on complex reasoning tasks through bounded rationality.

problem: Sparse Autoencoders for LLM interpretation lack rigorous mathematical guarantees and suffer from hyperparameter sensitivity and training instability.
approach: Introduces bias adaptation technique that adaptively adjusts neural network bias parameters to ensure appropriate activation sparsity, with theoretical recovery guarantees based on neuron resonance matching feature occurrence frequencies.
contribution: Provides the first SAE algorithm with theoretical feature recovery guarantees and demonstrates superior performance against benchmarks on LLMs up to 2 billion parameters.

problem: Deploying semantic segmentation in driving and robotics requires both real-time inference and robustness to domain shifts, but existing methods treat real-time and domain generalization separately.
approach: QPrompt-R1 injects learnable queries at the final transformer block with Group Relative Query Alignment objective that uses group-relative supervision to improve feature alignment without test-time overhead.
contribution: Achieves 54 FPS with strong performance in synthetic-to-real transfer and real-to-real generalization, improving state-of-the-art methods by 0.5-1.2% without inference-time cost.

problem: Integrating multimodal cellular screening data is challenging because biological signals partially overlap and cell-level pairing is frequently unavailable.
approach: PETRI uses early-fusion transformer with masked joint reconstruction and cross-modal attention to learn unified cell embeddings from unpaired cellular images and gene expression, grouping cells by shared context into multimodal documents.
contribution: Enables construction of perturbation-level profiles via simple averaging and reveals biologically meaningful multimodal concepts using sparse autoencoders.

problem: Developing fair classifiers under multiple group fairness constraints requires balancing multiple objectives like demographic parity, equalized odds, and predictive parity.
approach: Proposes post-processing approach that identifies optimal operating characteristics using group-wise ROC convex hulls and applies randomized mixture of thresholding rules to match targets while minimizing interventions.
contribution: Simultaneously satisfies approximate demographic parity, equalized odds, and predictive parity with few interventions and nearly optimal accuracy drop on standard benchmarks.

problem: Existing surrogate loss functions for disagreement discrepancy optimization are not Bayes consistent, potentially failing to maximize true disagreement when addressing distribution shift.
approach: Develops new surrogate losses with Bayes consistency guarantees and pairs cross-entropy with a novel disagreement loss to create a provably consistent surrogate for disagreement discrepancy.
contribution: Provides theoretical bounds on optimality gaps for surrogates and demonstrates more accurate and robust disagreement discrepancy estimates across benchmarks compared to existing approaches.

problem: Evaluating LLM progress is often constrained to verifiable tasks like math and programming, limiting assessment in professional domains requiring domain expert judgment.
approach: Introduces ProfBench with 7000+ response-criterion pairs evaluated by human experts and develops affordable LLM-Judges that mitigate self-enhancement bias and reduce evaluation cost by 2-3 orders of magnitude.
contribution: Reveals significant challenges in professional document processing where top models like GPT-5-high achieve only 65.9% performance, exposing disparities between proprietary and open-weight models.

problem: MoE-based LLMs rely on superficial safety mechanisms where harmful inputs route to safety-critical experts, but fine-tuning causes routing drift that exposes models to harmful attacks.
approach: SafeMoE penalizes the gap between routing weights of fine-tuned and safety-aligned models, preserving safety-aligned routing of harmful inputs to safety-critical experts.
contribution: Reduces harmfulness score from 62.0 to 5.0 on OLMoE while maintaining task utility within 1% degradation and 2% overhead, significantly outperforming defense methods.

problem: Few-step diffusion and flow-matching image generation models lack effective mechanisms for incorporating negative prompt guidance to suppress undesired content.
approach: VSF dynamically suppresses undesired content by flipping the sign of attention values from negative prompts, providing a simple and efficient method that integrates with MMDiT and cross-attention architectures.
contribution: Achieves 0.420-0.545 negative score on NegGenBench for quality settings, significantly outperforming prior methods at 0.320-0.380 while maintaining image and positive prompt quality.

problem: Video deraining suffers from motion artifacts and temporal mismatches from camera pose changes, with existing methods relying on expensive optical flow or heuristic alignment.
approach: DeLiVR injects spatiotemporal Lie-group differential biases into attention scores, using rotation-bounded Lie relative bias for frame alignment and differential group displacement to estimate velocity.
contribution: Achieves sharper details, fewer rain remnants, and stronger temporal coherence on synthetic and real rainy benchmarks through geometry-consistent Lie-group constraints.

problem: Self-supervised methods for articulated object modeling reconstruct discrete states with cross-state consistency, yielding fragmentation and drift that prevent smooth continuous control.
approach: PD²GS learns a shared canonical Gaussian field with arbitrary interaction states as its continuous deformations, jointly encoding geometry and kinematics with part-level decoupling.
contribution: Surpasses prior methods in geometric and kinematic accuracy and consistency under continuous control, supporting part-aware reconstruction without manual supervision.

problem: Cybersecurity operations require domain-specialized LLM assistants that don't expose sensitive data through proprietary APIs, but existing solutions lack domain adaptation.
approach: Curates 11.8B tokens of cybersecurity pretraining data and generates 266K multi-turn samples via agentic augmentation simulating expert workflows for supervised fine-tuning.
contribution: RedSage-8B surpasses baseline models by up to 5.59 points on cybersecurity benchmarks and 5.05 points on general tasks, providing locally deployable domain-aware assistant.

problem: Feed-forward networks in LLMs dominate parameters but their high-dimensional dynamics remain poorly understood, limiting insights into information organization and regulation.
approach: NerVE introduces lightweight eigenspectral framework tracking spectral entropy, participation ratio, early enrichment, and Jensen-Shannon divergence to understand FFN nonlinearity reshaping variance across eigenmodes.
contribution: Recovers stable spectral signatures correlating with generalization ability and responsive to architectural design choices, providing actionable insights for optimization.

problem: Dataset distillation for object detection remains largely unexplored compared to image classification, requiring methods that synthesize compact detection datasets from large-scale data.
approach: OD³ uses iterative candidate selection to place object instances in synthesized images based on suitable locations and candidate screening with pre-trained observers to remove low-confidence objects.
contribution: Achieves 14% improvement over prior best detection distillation at 1.0% compression ratio on MS COCO, establishing state-of-the-art results for detection dataset distillation.

problem: State-of-the-art model merging methods are evaluated on favorable benchmarks where robustness in realistic settings with disparate task vectors remains unexplored.
approach: DisTaC uses knowledge distillation to pre-condition problematic task vectors before merging, adjusting norms and increasing model confidence while preserving task-specific knowledge.
contribution: Enables state-of-the-art merging techniques to successfully integrate models exhibiting harmful traits where they would otherwise fail, achieving significant performance gains.
theme: Transfer Learning, Meta Learning, and Lifelong Learning

problem: Time-sensitive factual knowledge is difficult to evaluate in LLMs because existing benchmarks face manual bottlenecks limiting scalable and comprehensive TSQA evaluation.
approach: TDBench systematically constructs TSQA pairs using temporal databases, temporal functional dependencies, temporal SQL, and temporal joins, introducing time accuracy metric for fine-grained evaluation.
contribution: Enables scalable TSQA evaluation on application-specific temporal data while reducing human labor dependence, complementing Wikipedia/Wikidata-centric approaches.

problem: Modeling natural hand motions remains underexplored because existing methods rely on limited studio-captured datasets and struggle to capture animation fidelity with text-motion alignment.
approach: CLUTCH introduces 3D-HIW dataset of 32K hand-motion sequences with aligned text and proposes LLM-based system with SHIFT VQ-VAE for motion tokenization and geometric refinement for animation quality.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art on text-to-motion and motion-to-text tasks, establishing first benchmark for scalable in-the-wild hand motion modeling.

problem: Transformer attention mechanisms incur quadratic computation and memory costs with sequence length, creating major bottlenecks for long-context training in large language models.
approach: Proposes unified benchmark integrating representative attention kernels and context parallel mechanisms with modular interface evaluating methods across attention patterns and distributed scales.
contribution: Enables reproducible comparisons across up to 96 GPUs, highlights method-specific trade-offs, and provides practical guidance for deploying attention in long-context LLM training.

problem: Knowledge distillation may transfer test-set knowledge from contaminated teachers to clean students via data laundering, potentially threatening evaluation integrity.
approach: Systematically evaluates data laundering across eight benchmarks by comparing contamination effects with laundering magnitude, and studies train-test distribution gaps.
contribution: Finds laundering is rare and statistically insignificant in most cases, demonstrating knowledge distillation functions as effective decontamination that largely mitigates test-data leakage.
theme: Transfer Learning, Meta Learning, and Lifelong Learning

problem: Rotary Positional Embedding causes performance breakdown when input length exceeds training length, with unclear mechanistic understanding of how extra rotation causes pathological behavior.
approach: Proposes RoPE-ID that applies RoPE with high frequency to a subset of channels, preserving attention's key/query cluster separation and sink token functionality for longer inputs.
contribution: Enables attention to generalize to longer inputs out-of-box with simple modification, demonstrated on LongBench and RULER benchmarks with 1B and 3B models.

problem: Sparse-reward exploration in reinforcement learning is inefficient and leads to brittle policies in dynamic environments.
approach: Introduces graph-based intrinsic reward using Effective Resistance from spectral graph theory to guide agents toward configurations correlated with successful goal-reaching states.
contribution: Demonstrates improvements up to 59% in success rate and 56% in timesteps with theoretical variance reduction guarantees, outperforming state-of-the-art baselines.

problem: Solving high-dimensional mean-field games remains challenging due to fundamental computational and analytical obstacles in finding Nash equilibria with continuum of agents.
approach: Proposes particle-based deep Flow-Matching method where particles are updated using first-order information and flow neural network is trained to match sample trajectory velocities in simulation-free manner.
contribution: Proves convergence to stationary points sublinearly and linear/exponential under convexity, demonstrates promising performance on non-potential MFGs and high-dimensional optimal transport.

problem: Learning heuristics for A* search often disregards admissibility guarantees needed for optimal solutions and provides limited generalization guarantees beyond training data.
approach: Poses heuristic learning as constrained optimization with Cross-Entropy Admissibility loss enforcing admissibility during training, leveraging PDB abstractions for generalization bounds.
contribution: Yields heuristics with near-perfect admissibility and stronger guidance than PDB, providing first generalization guarantees for goal-dependent heuristics with bounds depending on network width and depth.

problem: Long document summarization challenges LLMs with information loss, factual inconsistencies, and coherence issues when processing excessively long documents.
approach: SummQ uses adversarial multi-agent framework where summary and quiz generators collaborate through competitive feedback loops, with examinee agent validating if summary contains information needed for quiz answers.
contribution: Significantly outperforms state-of-the-art on three benchmarks across ROUGE, BERTScore, LLM-as-a-Judge, and human evaluations through multi-agent collaboration.

problem: Coding-agent benchmarks assume infinite tokens and resources, but production deployments face hard costs per LLM call, test, and rollback decision.
approach: USACOArena introduces ICPC-inspired arena where agents pay deterministic credits for every action, exposing decision profiles and cost-benefit trade-offs under budget constraints.
contribution: Reveals rich policy space where identically seeded agents diverge in self-play, showing importance of over-specialization tax and lightweight scaffolding ROI for budget-aware coding agents.

problem: Long-horizon reasoning in Vision-Language-Action agents suffers from cascading failures when intermediate actions are mis-specified without flexible correction mechanisms.
approach: ReCAPA uses predictive correction at three levels (actions, subgoals, trajectories) with semantic alignment via Sinkhorn-based and Score-field modules to adjust representations during training.
contribution: Achieves competitive results on embodied agent benchmarks, outperforming proprietary and open-source LLM baselines while introducing metrics to quantify error propagation and recovery.

problem: RL training for LLM reasoning oscillates between entropy collapse and entropy explosion when using mean-baseline value-free RL methods.
approach: Quantile Advantage Estimation replaces mean with group-wise K-quantile baseline inducing response-level two-regime gate, with theoretical two-sided entropy safety bounds.
contribution: Stabilizes entropy while sparsifying credit assignment and yielding sustained pass@1 gains on AIME/AMC benchmarks, demonstrating baseline design as primary scaling mechanism.

problem: Fine-tuning datasets are designed at sentence-level but token-level optimization causes noise that harms LLM performance.
approach: XTF decomposes token-level contributions into three attributes (reasoning importance, knowledge novelty, task relevance) and masks gradients of noisy tokens accordingly.
contribution: Improves downstream performance by up to 13.7% across math, code, and medicine tasks on seven mainstream LLMs through token-level attribute decomposition.

problem: MLLMs excel at visual comprehension but struggle to extract mathematical models from technical diagrams, lacking evaluation of the complete engineering workflow from perception to design.
approach: CircuitSense introduces benchmark with 8,006+ problems spanning component to system-level circuits, synthetic generation pipeline with auto-derived equations, and hierarchical evaluation.
contribution: Reveals closed-source models achieve 85%+ on perception but below 19% on symbolic derivation, exposing critical gap between visual parsing and mathematical reasoning in engineering domains.

problem: Visual representation processing in dynamic environments requires decoupling motion and color perception, but lacks effective methods integrating multi-modal visual inputs.
approach: SpikeGen emulates human visual system by integrating decomposed RGB and spike camera inputs with latent-space generative frameworks, addressing spatial sparsity in spikes and temporal sparsity in RGB.
contribution: Demonstrates synergistic enhancement of visual modalities on spike-RGB tasks including deblurring, frame reconstruction, and high-speed novel-view synthesis.

problem: Large language models remain vulnerable to jailbreak attacks that bypass safety guardrails, with defenses based on adversarial training failing against novel attacks.
approach: Proposes Adversarial Skill Compositional Training that trains on diverse compositions of extracted adversarial skill primitives from 32 attack papers rather than isolated instances.
contribution: Substantially improves robustness to unseen attacks including multi-turn jailbreaks while maintaining low over-refusal rates, with novel attacks explainable as sparse skill compositions.
